text:
dev-docs: Kicking off a small refresh for the 'sparkkit' onboarding tutorial this sprint. Goals: simplify auth guidance, add a one-file docker example for first-deploy, and modernize the Node + Py snippets to SDK 6+. Keeping PRs tiny for fast reviews.
anya: nice. Can you share which pages will change? I want to update the screenshots if layout shifts.
dev-docs: pages: /docs/get-started/sparkkit, /docs/sdk/node/quickstart, /docs/sdk/python/quickstart. Also the troubleshooting section for token rotation.
marcus: Ill own the screenshots and the tiny UX copy edits. Short ask: keep screenshots to 800x450 and annotate the env section only.
ben: I'll do the docker example. Proposal: single Dockerfile + run script instead of a multi-service compose. Less noise for first-timers. Sample run in docs will map port and pass env via --env-file.
rachel: I can migrate Node examples to SDK6. Will also add a short streaming note and link to the streaming guide rather than expand in place.
qa-bot: checklist: run smoke tests in staging after merge. Please add a smoke test that hits /health and a simple generate call.
dev-docs: suggested Node snippet for docs (one-liner compact):

```js
import Redwood from '@redwood/inference';
const cli = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
const out = await cli.generate({ model: 'clarion-mini', prompt: 'Welcome' });
console.log(out.text);
```

dev-docs: will call out that streaming differs and link to /docs/streaming. Also will add Windows shell examples for env export.
anya: for the token rotation troubleshooting row, include the common symptom + quick fix: "check token in secret manager, restart process, flush local env in CI".
ben: Dockerfile I'm adding to the repo:

```Dockerfile
FROM node:18-alpine
WORKDIR /app
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci --production
COPY . .
CMD ["node","index.js"]
```

ben: run script example in docs: `docker build -t sparkkit . && docker run --env-file .env -p 3000:3000 sparkkit`
marcus: for screenshots, I'll replace the header screenshot that references "API Key" with a small panel showing the env table. Keep copy short: "set REDWOOD_API_KEY in your shell" -> expanded to show mac/linux and windows commands.
rachel: Python minimal example will include both curl and SDK usage. Curl example: `curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" -d '{"model":"clarion-mini","prompt":"hi"}'` and then a short SDK snippet.
anya: one tiny UX nit: the docs earlier used `REDWOOD_API_HOST` and `REDWOOD_REGION` inconsistently. Can we standardize on host + region note for Private deployments?
dev-docs: agree. We'll add a "When you run Private or Dedicated" box explaining differences (use REDWOOD_API_HOST, and Dedicated may require X-Account-ID header).

ci-bot: PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4601 - "snippets: node & python sdk6 migration" by rachel
anya: I'll review 4599 for copy and screenshots. Please include the original image files in the PR branch.
marcus: uploaded annotated screenshots to the PR branch (pngs).
ben: added a tiny smoke script tests/smoke.sh that curls /health and a minimal generate call with retries (3x).
dev-docs: request ordering: merge 4599 first (copy + env table) so snippet and docker PRs can rebase with the canonical env names.
ci-bot: PR 4599 ready for merge after 1 approval.
rachel: rebased snippet PR after 4599 merged locally. Updated Node example to show minimal error handling and a one-line comment about async/await.
anya: approved 4599 with screenshot suggestions.
ci-bot: PR 4599 merged by dev-docs at 1765009920
ben: rebased 4600, smoke.sh passes in my local container run. Opened a follow-up to shorten the health check timeout per qa suggestion.
qa-bot: ran smoke job in staging; health check failed once due to flakey network but second attempt passed. Logging note added.
dev-docs: final checklist before closing: docs copy + screenshots done, docker run + smoke done, node+py snippets done, private/dedicated callout added. I'll prepare a short release note and tag the onboarding-team channel.
anya: thanks all  looks neat.
